prompt: Manage a GitHub repository workflow: authenticate, inspect organization/repository access, create and label pull requests, inspect CI and workflow logs, merge approved changes, dispatch build/deploy/destroy workflows, and troubleshoot deployment failures.

results.use_case: Manage a GitHub repository workflow: authenticate, inspect organization/repository access, create and label pull requests, inspect CI and workflow logs, merge approved changes, dispatch build/deploy/destroy workflows, and troubleshoot deployment failures.
results.execution_guidance: IMPORTANT: Follow the recommended plan below. Extract steps before execution, adapt to your current context, execute sequentially with current_step parameter, and check known pitfalls to avoid errors.
recommended_plan_steps: [Required] [Prerequisite]: Collect/confirm owner, repo, head branch, and base branch; verify branch names exist using GITHUB_LIST_BRANCHES (prevent typos before PR/merge/delete).
[Optional (if unsure there are commits to merge)] [Prerequisite]: Preflight base↔head changes using GITHUB_COMPARE_TWO_COMMITS (avoid creating a PR with no diff).
[Optional (if you need to locate an existing PR first)] [Prerequisite]: Find relevant PRs using GITHUB_FIND_PULL_REQUESTS (to reuse/merge the right PR).
[Optional (if GITHUB_FIND_PULL_REQUESTS is insufficient)] [Fallback]: Broaden discovery using GITHUB_SEARCH_ISSUES_AND_PULL_REQUESTS (use scoped qualifiers; handle pagination).
[Required] [Step]: Create a pull request from head into base using GITHUB_CREATE_A_PULL_REQUEST (clear title/body summarizing changes).

[Optional (if tracking/discussion is needed)] [Next Step]: Create/augment a tracking ticket using GITHUB_CREATE_AN_ISSUE and coordinate via GITHUB_CREATE_AN_ISSUE_COMMENT (links, next actions, conflict notes).
[Required (after explicit user confirmation)] [Step]: Merge the pull request using GITHUB_MERGE_A_PULL_REQUEST (select merge method).
[Required] [Fallback]: If merge fails/not mergeable, inspect status/details using GITHUB_GET_A_PULL_REQUEST, resolve conflicts outside tools as needed, then retry GITHUB_MERGE_A_PULL_REQUEST.
[Required (after verifying base has desired changes + explicit user confirmation)] [Next Step]: Delete obsolete remote branches using GITHUB_DELETE_A_REFERENCE (one call per branch).
known_pitfalls: [GITHUB_CREATE_A_PULL_REQUEST] HTTP 422 “No commits between base and head” when branches have no diff; validate with GITHUB_COMPARE_TWO_COMMITS and/or pick correct head/base.
[GITHUB_MERGE_A_PULL_REQUEST] May return 405 when the pull request is not mergeable; resolve conflicts before retrying.
[GITHUB_GET_A_PULL_REQUEST] Can surface very large diffs; fetch only what you need for mergeability/context to avoid heavy processing.
[GITHUB_DELETE_A_REFERENCE] Deleting branches before confirming the merge/removal path is correct removes an easy rollback option.
[GITHUB_SEARCH_ISSUES_AND_PULL_REQUESTS] Rate-limited and paginated; poorly scoped queries can trigger 403 errors if backoff/Retry-After is ignored.

GITHUB_CREATE_A_PULL_REQUEST.description: Creates a pull request in a GitHub repository, requiring existing `base` and `head` branches; `title` or `issue` must be provided.

base.description: The name of the branch you want the changes pulled into. This must be an existing branch on the current (target) repository. You cannot submit a pull request to one repository that requests a merge to a base branch of another repository.

examples: This PR introduces a new feature that does X, Y, and Z.
Fixes #42 by addressing the off-by-one error.
body.description: The detailed description or contents of the pull request.

head.description: The name of the branch where your changes are implemented. IMPORTANT: This branch must already exist in the repository (or fork) before calling this action. You must first create the branch and push commits to it (using git or the 'Create a reference' action), then create the PR. For cross-repository pull requests, namespace `head` with the source owner and branch, like `username:branch`.

repo.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This name is not case-sensitive.

draft.description: Indicates whether the pull request should be created as a draft. Draft pull requests cannot be merged until marked as ready for review.

issue.description: The number of an existing issue in the repository to convert into a pull request. If provided, the issue's title and body may be used for the pull request. Required if `title` is not specified.

owner.description: The account owner of the repository. This name is not case-sensitive.

title.description: The title of the new pull request. Required unless `issue` is specified.

head_repo.description: The name of the repository (e.g., 'octocat/Hello-World') where the changes in the pull request were made. This field is required for cross-repository pull requests if both the source and target repositories are owned by the same organization but are different repositories.

maintainer_can_modify.description: Indicates whether maintainers of the upstream repository can modify the pull request. This is primarily relevant for pull requests originating from forks.

GITHUB_MERGE_A_PULL_REQUEST.description: Merges an open and mergeable pull request in a repository. A 405 error can occur for multiple reasons: (1) The PR is still in draft mode - convert it to ready-for-review first using GITHUB_UPDATE_A_PULL_REQUEST. (2) Branch protection rules are not satisfied - check for required approving reviews, status checks, or other repository rules that must be met before merging. (3) The base branch has been modified since the PR was last synced - update the PR branch first using GITHUB_UPDATE_A_PULL_REQUEST_BRANCH.

sha.description: SHA of the pull request's head commit. Must match for merge to succeed, ensuring PR hasn't changed since review.

repo.description: Repository name, without the `.git` extension. Not case-sensitive.

pull_number.description: The unique number identifying the pull request. The PR must be mergeable: not a draft, and all branch protection rules (required reviews, status checks, etc.) must be satisfied.

examples: Fixing a typo in the README file
commit_title.description: Title for the merge commit message.

merge_method.description: Merge strategy: 'merge', 'squash', or 'rebase'. Defaults to repository's setting if unspecified.

examples: This change updates the project description to be more accurate.
commit_message.description: Additional details for the merge commit message.

GITHUB_CREATE_AN_ISSUE.description: Creates a new issue in a GitHub repository, requiring the repository to exist and have issues enabled; specific fields like assignees, milestone, or labels may require push access.

examples: Detailed description of the bug with steps to reproduce.
I think adding a dark mode would improve user experience...
body.description: The detailed textual contents of the new issue.

repo.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension (case-insensitive). The repository must exist, be accessible, and have issues enabled.

owner.description: The GitHub account owner of the repository (case-insensitive). The repository must exist and be accessible to the authenticated user.

title.description: The title for the new issue.

labels.description: Array of label names to associate with this issue (generally case-insensitive). NOTE: Only users with push access can set labels; they are silently dropped otherwise. Pass an empty list to clear all labels.

assignee.description: Login for the user to whom this issue should be assigned. NOTE: Only users with push access can set the assignee; it is silently dropped otherwise. **This field is deprecated in favor of `assignees`.**

assignees.description: GitHub login names for users to assign to this issue. NOTE: Only users with push access can set assignees; they are silently dropped otherwise.

milestone.description: The ID of the milestone to associate this issue with (e.g., "5"). NOTE: Only users with push access can set the milestone; it is silently dropped otherwise.

GITHUB_CREATE_AN_ISSUE_COMMENT.description: Creates a new comment on an existing GitHub issue or pull request within the specified repository.

body.description: Comment content in GitHub Flavored Markdown.

repo.description: Name of the repository (without `.git` extension); not case-sensitive.

owner.description: Account owner of the repository (username or organization); not case-sensitive.

issue_number.description: Number identifying the issue or pull request for the comment.

GITHUB_LIST_BRANCHES.description: List branches in a GitHub repository. Returns branch names, commit information, and protection status. Use this action when you need to retrieve all branches in a repository, optionally filtered by protection status. This is useful for identifying available branches, checking which branches are protected, or preparing to create pull requests.

page.description: The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see 'Using pagination in the REST API'.

repo.description: The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.

owner.description: The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.

per_page.description: The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see 'Using pagination in the REST API'.

protected.description: Setting to `true` returns only branches protected by branch protections or rulesets. When set to `false`, only unprotected branches are returned. Omitting this parameter returns all branches.
